Bug_Title: Eq: Covariant equals() method defined, Object.equals(Object) inherited (EQ_SELF_USE_OBJECT)
Bug_Details:
This class defines a covariant version of the equals()
method, but inherits the normal equals(Object) method
defined in the base java.lang.Object class. 
The class should probably define a boolean equals(Object) method.
 equals() equals(Object) java.lang.Object boolean equals(Object)
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by defining a covariant version of the equals() method (equals(CovariantEqualsExample other)) instead of overriding the Object.equals(Object) method. This causes issues when comparing objects of the same class but passed as Object type.
Trigger_Explanation: The test calls the showBug method of the CovariantEqualsExample class. Inside showBug, obj1.equals(obj3) is called where obj3 is of type Object. Since the equals method is not overridden for Object type, it defaults to Object.equals(Object), which does not compare the values correctly, thus triggering the bug.
